title: Hydrophobic Durability of Butterfly Wing Surfaces after Freezing Cycles
author: Tingkun Chen
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.i2mcgc6
materials: Avoid the surface of copper sheet from scratching.

steps.title: Acquire and Classify Butterfly Specimens
steps.instruction: Purchase butterfly specimens from Yunnan Aegean Sea Butterfly and verify they are not protected species and are correctly classified using systematic taxonomy.

substeps.instruction: Verify specimens against the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora and the Series of the National Zoological Museum of China for wilding Ecology and Conservation-Butterflies.

Complete final classification using Systematic Butterfly Names of the World, Series of the National Zoological Museum of China for wilding Ecology and Conservation-Butterflies, and Classification and Identification of Chinese Butterflies.
Store specimens in a glass box with air flow.

steps.title: Prepare Copper Sheets
steps.instruction: Manufacture and clean copper sheets to serve as substrates.

substeps.instruction: Slice 0.5mm thick copper plates (from Xingye Copper International Group Limited) into sheets with a diameter of 6mm.
Ensure edges are flanged and surfaces are not scratched.
Clean sheets in an acetone ultrasonic bath for 5 min.
Clean sheets in a deionized water ultrasonic bath for 5 min.
Dry sheets in an oven at 60 ℃.

steps.title: Prepare Butterfly Wing Samples
steps.instruction: Extract wing sections from anesthetized butterflies.

substeps.instruction: Anesthetize the butterfly specimen using ether (from Beijing Chemical Works).
Cut the butterfly wing using a scalpel.

steps.title: Mount Wings to Copper Sheets
steps.instruction: Attach the wing specimens to the prepared copper substrates.

substeps.instruction: Paste butterfly wing specimens onto the copper sheets using 3M 8810 thermal conductor adhesive tape.
Verify the flatness of the specimens using a horizontal microscope.
Remove surface impurities using dry nitrogen.

steps.title: Perform Baseline Surface Characterization
steps.instruction: Analyze the initial morphology and hydrophobicity of the wings.

substeps.instruction: Observe surface morphology using Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM).
Measure the contact angle using the OCA 20 contact angle measurement system (Amount: μl).

steps.title: Conduct Freezing Cycle Experiments
steps.instruction: Expose samples to freezing conditions and analyze the resulting durability.

substeps.instruction: Adjust experimental apparatus to the determined temperature and humidity.
Record the frosting process on the sample surfaces using an observation device.
Clean the sample with dry nitrogen after each experiment.
Observe the micro-structure using AFM.
Measure the contact angle using the OCA 20 (Amount: μl), ensuring the operational temperature of the OCA 20 is below 25 ℃.
